in_arabic.name: رقيب
in_arabic.long_meaning: رقيب (raqīb) کا مطلب ہے کوئی ایسا شخص جو کسی چیز کی نگرانی کرتا ہے، حفاظت کرتا ہے یا مراقبت کرتا ہے۔ یہ نام اللہ کے 99 ناموں (اسماء الحسنیٰ) میں سے ایک ہے، جس میں رقيب بھی شامل ہے جس کا مطلب ہے 'نگران' یا 'مراقب'۔ قرآن میں رقيب کا ذکر سورة آل عمران میں ہوا ہے۔

in_urdu.name: رقیب
in_urdu.long_meaning: رقیب (raqīb) کا مطلب ہے کوئی ایسا شخص جو کسی چیز کی نگرانی کرتا ہے، حفاظت کرتا ہے یا مراقبت کرتا ہے۔ یہ نام عربی جڑوں سے نکلا ہے، جہاں 'ر-ق-ب' کا مطلب ہے 'نگرانی کرنا' یا 'دیکھنا'۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلم روایت میں، یہ نام روحانی اہمیت رکھتا ہے کیونکہ یہ اللہ کی خصوصیات میں سے ایک کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: रकीब
in_hindi.long_meaning: रकीब (Raqīb) का अर्थ है कोई ऐसा व्यक्ति जो किसी चीज़ की निगरानी करता है, उसकी रक्षा करता है या देखभाल करता है। यह नाम अरबी जड़ों से निकला है, जहाँ 'र-क़-ब' का अर्थ है 'निगरानी करना' या 'देखना'। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम आध्यात्मिक महत्व रखता है क्योंकि यह अल्लाह की विशेषताओं में से एक को प्रकट करता है।

in_pashto.name: رقيب
in_pashto.meaning: د ليدن ساتونکی، څوک چې څه باندې نظارت کوي
in_pashto.long_meaning: رقيب (raqīb) د هغه چا معنی دی چې د څه په نظارت کوي، حفاظت یې کوي یا مواظبت کوي. دا نوم د پښتو کلتور او د افغان او پښتنو دودیزو مسلمو ارزښتونو برخه ده، چیرته چې 'ر-ق-ب' د 'نظارت' یا 'لید' معنی لري.

in_english.name: Raqueeb
in_english.meaning: one who watches, observes, or guards
in_english.long_meaning: Raqueeb (Raqīb) originates from the Arabic root 'r-q-b', meaning 'to watch', 'to observe', or 'to guard'. It is one of Allah's 99 names (Asma'ul-Husna), signifying 'the Watcher' or 'the Guardian'. In Islamic tradition, Raqueeb is mentioned in the Quran, specifically in Surah Al-Imran. The name holds significant spiritual meaning, reflecting the attribute of Allah as the vigilant and protective entity. Across Muslim cultures, Raqueeb is used as a given name, symbolizing the desirable qualities of vigilance, protection, and care.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Raqueeb" in Islamic culture holds a profound meaning and significance, particulary in the Arab world. The name can be traced back to the Arabic language, where 'Raqib' or 'Raqqab' means ‘rider’ or ‘mounted warrior.’ Historically, this name has been given to individuals who were accomplished horsemen or warriors who led their armies into battle. Considered a source of honor and pride, a warrior named Raqueeb would have been respectably placed among his peers and highly regarded in his community. Today, the name reflects a sense of leadership, courage, and adventure.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, 'Raqueeb' represents a journey through life with commitment, determination, and resilience. The name suggests a traveler on the path to God, constantly seeking knowledge, growth, and enlightenment. In fact, the root of the word 'Raqueeb' (qab) appears in several Quranic verses that refer to being constant and steadfast in one’s faith. For example, in Surah Al-Hajj (22:35), it is stated, “And We made them [Ibrahim and his descendants] Imams guiding [by Our Law] by [Our] contact and We were certainly gracious to them.” The term 'Imam,' the spiritual leader of the Muslim community, is derived from the same root as 'Raqueeb' - the one who travels the spiritual path and gathers others on the same journey towards Allah. Ultimately, the name embodies a constant endeavor towards self-improvement and closeness to Allah SWT.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldoon's 'The Muqaddimah'. In the chapter on 'The Bedouins' and their role in the formation of the Islamic State, Ibn Khaldoon mentions a tribe named Raqueeb. He describes them as a leading Bedouin tribe during the time of the Prophet Muhammad (6th century CE) and the Rashidun Caliphs (7th century CE).

historical_references.reference: Al-Baladhuri's 'Ansab Al-Ashraf'. This historical work mentions Raqueeb as one of the major tribes of Kindah, a confederation of Arab tribes that played a significant role in the early Islamic era (7th-8th centuries CE). The Raqueeb tribe is noted for its military prowess and its alliance with the Islamic forces against the Sassanid and Byzantine empires.
